newsitem.title: UK: IBCA says UK electric sector strong, may cut.
newsitem.headline: IBCA says UK electric sector strong, may cut.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said in a report on Monday that the underlying creditworthiness of the British electricity sector remained strong.
It assigned a number of ratings and affirmed ratings on two companies, but it also said it may downgrade one company, Northern Electric Plc.

In the report, a long-term rating of AA and a short-term of A1 plus have been assigned to each of the following Regional Electricity Companies (RECs): East Midlands Electricity Plc, London Electricity Plc, Southern Electric Plc and Yorkshire Electricity Group Plc, IBCA said.
Northern Electric Plc is assigned a long-term rating of A and a short-term rating of A1, and placed on RatingWatch with negative implications, IBCA said.
Norweb Plc's and SWALEC Plc's short- and long-term ratings of A1 and A plus respectively are affirmed, IBCA said.

"Northern Electric's rating reflects the substantial impact of the 500 million stg plus shareholder value package that formed part of its defence against a hostile takeover bid from Trafalgar House Plc in 1994," IBCA said in a statement.

"Returns to shareholders have almost halved Northern's equity base over the past two years. At the same time, ongoing commitments to future dividend payments threaten to see coverages fall further, against a background of reduced profitability," IBCA said.

"In addition, in light of the current takeover bid launched by US utility CalEnergy , we are placing Northern's ratings on RatingWatch with negative implications, pending the outcome of the bid," IBCA said.
RECs operate in a monopoly environment for high-margin distribution business, and will not face full competition in low-margin power supply operations until 1998, according to IBCA.

IBCA has taken on board several considerations - including the likely stagnation in earnings implied by regulatory revenue cuts in distribution, the potential for future deficits in the supply business on full deregulation, and the increased capital expenditure burdens to 2000 - but considers that the strong cash generation and minimal business risk of distribution activities will continue to support ratings for independent RECs in the AA category, it said.

In the case of RECs acquired by water utilities, it is IBCA's view that a material difference exists between the ring-fencing provisions introduced by the electricity regulator and those of his counterpart in the water industry, IBCA said.

"Specifically, the absence of an explicit restriction on dividend upstreaming in the modified electricity licence potentially exposes the REC to a disproportionate share of the group financing burden," IBCA said.
This risk has been reflected in the ratings for SWALEC Plc and Norweb Plc, it added.

Two principal event risks have been taken into account in assigning ratings: the extension of competitive supply to 22 million domestic households in April 1998 and the threat of a windfall tax under a future Labour government, IBCA said.
IBCA has considered the potential effects of both, on the following assumptions.

"Supply represents only a small portion of REC profits and a projected fall-off in contributions from this area should not have a substantial impact on the overall profitability of the sector," IBCA said.
Against this, there is a strong likelihood that full deregulation will be delayed by more than the three months recently conceded by the regulator, IBCA said.
IBCA has based its ratings on the assumption of minimal profit levels, or small losses, on supply operations until 2000.
With regard to the possibility of a windfall tax, IBCA has projected the impact of a levy with a hypothetical cost to the 12 RECs and two Gencos of three billion stg.

"On current performance, the agency believes the RECs could survive a levy on this scale at their current ratings. It would therefore not anticipate a sector downgrade in the event of a Labour victory between now and May 1997," IBCA said.
Each company would, however, be reviewed on its own merits, and more Draconian levels of retrospective taxation would see downward pressure on the entire sector's ratings, it said.
IBCA intends to publish ratings on the two generating companies, National Power Plc and PowerGen Plc, later this year.
